A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same agentic plan-caching framework. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, algorithms and appendices support comparison despite changes in title, authorship and formatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original FinanceBench and TabMWP experiments, including cost, accuracy, cache-search analyses and model-sensitivity results.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds benchmark results, latency measurements, cache-management analyses and cold-start measurements.

M1.justification: The core workflow, Algorithms 1–3 and appendix prompts remain unchanged. However, v2 implements optional fuzzy keyword retrieval and LRU eviction, previously left for future work, and reports automatic caching disablement when hit rates remain low.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained FinanceBench and TabMWP coverage, v2 evaluates QASPER scientific-document questions, AIME 2024/2025 mathematics and GAIA tasks involving multi-step reasoning and tool use. This substantially broadens the evaluated domains and task requirements.

E2.justification: The four original named baselines and their participation in the retained benchmark comparisons are unchanged. Tables 5–6 add a fuzzy keyword-retrieval alternative evaluated against default exact matching. The added benchmark and latency comparisons otherwise use the existing accuracy-optimal and cost-optimal controls.

E3.justification: v2 adds a wall-clock benchmark using 100 randomly sampled FinanceBench queries, LRU cache-capacity sweeps, lookup timing up to one million entries, fuzzy-threshold experiments and cold-start tracking. GAIA uses Open Deep Research with GPT-4o/GPT-4o-mini. The original 200-question FinanceBench and TabMWP evaluation settings remain documented unchanged.

E4.justification: New Sections 4.3–4.5 analyze latency by component, cache-capacity saturation, exact versus fuzzy lookup scalability, fuzzy-matching accuracy tradeoffs and cache warm-up. These substantially extend the operational sensitivity analysis. Existing cache-hit/miss comparisons and Appendix C model-sensitivity studies are retained.

E5.justification: v2 explicitly reports averaging cache-lookup measurements over 100 trials in Section 4.4 and Table 5; v1 provides no corresponding repeated-trial reporting. Neither version supplies defined error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests for the main cost/accuracy results, despite v2's affirmative checklist statement.

E6.justification: The original benchmark plots, cost breakdown and Appendix C numerical results are unchanged. v2 adds substantial results: Table 1 reports GAIA APC cost/accuracy of $16.27/36.97%, versus $69.02/37.58% for the accuracy-optimal baseline; Table 3 reports FinanceBench latency of 1424.82 versus 1959.24 seconds. Tables 4–7 add cache-management findings. Revised headline aggregates cover expanded experiments rather than demonstrating a same-setting improvement over v1.

T1.justification: Neither version contains substantive theoretical results, proofs or formal derivations. The appendix algorithms and worked-example mathematics are unchanged; v2's standard dictionary lookup complexity statement does not introduce a new theoretical contribution.

C1.justification: The main contribution expands from cost reduction on two workloads to cost and latency reduction across five workload groups and two agent architectures. The abstract and conclusion replace 46.62% cost reduction with 50.31%, add a 27.28% latency-reduction claim, and revise reported accuracy retention from 96.67% to 96.61%.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations concerning GAIA's limited initial keyword reuse but useful replanning reuse, cache saturation near the number of unique task keywords, fuzzy matching's relevance/efficiency tradeoff, and cold-start overhead with possible offline prewarming. The earlier limitations and societal-impact discussion are retained in Appendix E rather than removed.

D1.justification: v2 specifies Python dictionary lookup, the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 fuzzy matcher and semantic-caching thresholds of 80%, 85% and 90%. Main-text Llama-3.2-8B references become Llama-3.1-8B, matching v1's appendices rather than establishing a model change. Hardware, API versions/prices, prompts and the promised future code release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 adds a focused comparison with classic case-based planning, distinguishing automatic LLM template extraction from symbolic planning. v2 also adds benchmark, agent-memory, context-caching and social-simulation references and removes Mind2Web. The existing positioning around serving efficiency rather than enhanced agent capability largely remains.

P1.justification: The title and terminology adopt APC and test-time memory, and the abstract and concluding summary are updated. The Discussion becomes a Conclusion, with most discussion text moved verbatim to Appendix E; acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist are added. Most existing explanatory prose and appendix content remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds six experimental tables, retains but rescales and relocates Figures 1–5, and reformats the document in NeurIPS style. The appendix algorithms and model-sensitivity tables are consolidated into denser layouts. These are substantial display and layout changes beyond table renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's narrow validation and untested deployment behavior through additional domains, a second agent architecture, measured latency, and cache-capacity, retrieval and cold-start analyses. These strengthen evidence for practical applicability and expose operating tradeoffs. Important limitations remain: the headline latency wording exceeds the single FinanceBench microbenchmark's scope, and Appendix B lacks dataset-specific setup for the added benchmarks. These weaknesses qualify, but do not outweigh, the substantial evidential gains.
